newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican organic coffee group seeks trading partner.
newsitem.headline: Mexican organic coffee group seeks trading partner.

text.p: Coffee growers from the state of Guerrero, bidding to shake off Mexico's poor quality bean image, seek a long-term trading partnership to market their organic beans under the trade name Paradise Coffee.
Eight growers groups have formed the Self-Sustaining Producers Network, known in Spanish as RASA, to promote Paradise Coffee, RASA spokesman Arturo Garcia said.

RASA, which comprises 450 growers, directly produces around 450 tonnes of green coffee per cycle (7,500 60-kilo bags). It also indirectly buys up 1,800 tonnes (30,000 60-kg bags) from 22 nearby Guerrero communities.
Garcia said all the communities that grow coffee on this western flank of the Sierra Madre Occidental use ecological growing systems and are certified organic producers.

One of Mexico's middle ranking growing regions, Guerrero coffee is produced along the mountains that overlook the resort of Ixtapa Zihuatanejo to the tourist center of Acapulco, with peak state production around Atoyac de Alvarez.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
